newsitem.title: USA: Former U.S. representative named to EBRD board.
newsitem.headline: Former U.S. representative named to EBRD board.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Friday named Karen Shepherd, a former U.S. representative from Utah, to serve the U.S. executive director on the board of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).

The White House said in a statement that the nomination was a "recess appointment," meaning that it was put forward while Congress was out of session and thereby avoids the legal requirement for the Senate to approve it.
Under a recess appointment, the person in question may serve until the end of the next legislative session, which in this case would be late 1998.
The White House said it would submit Shepherd's nomination when the next Congress takes office at the start of 1997, thereby giving the Senate the opportunity to act on it.
The EBRD is a London-based development bank founded by Western governments to help the former Communist states of Eastern Europe make the transition to capitalism.
